extracts.title: Honble Governors Address in the Legislative Assembly on 21st June 2021
extracts.text:
Covid in Tamil Nadu. Corporate

entities, small businesses, traders’ groups,

non-governmental organisations, political

parties, artistes and volunteers are working

shoulder to shoulder with the Government

machinery in combating the pandemic.

So far, Rs.335.01 crore have poured in as

contributions to the Chief Minister’s Public

Relief Fund from various quarters, and of this

Rs.141.10 crore has been immediately and

transparently utilized for procurement of the

most essential life-saving drugs and medical

equipment. A further amount of Rs.50 crore

will be allotted for augmenting the supply of

Liquid Medical Oxygen to Government

hospitals and Rs.50 crore for preparatory

9

activities for the anticipated third wave of

Covid.

12) Conscious of the need to

preserve livelihoods in the middle of the

pandemic and to provide succour to the

people suffering from loss of income, this

Government disbursed Rs.4,000 as relief

assistance in two instalments, totaling

Rs.8,393 crore to all 2.1 crore rice ration

card holders in the State in May and June.

Many leading economists in the world have

emphasized that when the economy has

been greatly impacted by the pandemic,

direct cash relief assistance to the poor is the

most appropriate policy response. This

initiative of the Government of Tamil Nadu is

in keeping with such prescriptions and will

stimulate consumer demand and help the

economic cycle return to normalcy. Further,

10

grocery kits worth Rs.466 each, containing

14 essential commodities have also been

provided to all rice ration card holders at a

total cost of Rs.977.11 crore. Additional

5 kilos of rice for each person in the family is

being provided to all rice card holders in the

State for the months of May and June at an

additional cost of Rs.687.84 crore to the

State Government. In keeping with

Perarignar Anna’s immortal words, that

“we will see God in the smile of the poor”,

a total amount of Rs.10,068 crore has been

provided as livelihood assistance so far by

this Government after assumption of office.

13) Medical experts have warned of a

third wave of Covid. This Government will

take all necessary measures to counter the

possible third wave. Health infrastructure is

being further strengthened. All the ongoing

11

construction projects in the health sector,

including that of the eleven new

medical colleges are being expedited for

early completion. A new 500 bedded

multi-specialty hospital will be constructed in

the King Institute campus, Chennai at a total

cost of Rs.250 crore. Oxygen storage and

35) One of the first five orders of

this Government was the reduction in retail

price of Aavin milk by Rs.3 per litre, which

greatly benefited middle-class families. As a

result, the sale of Aavin milk in the entire

State has increased by about 1.5 lakh

litres per day.

36) The supply of free rice to each

ration card will be continued. All eligible

persons who apply for a ration card will be

provided a smart card within fifteen days.

The procurement of commodities like pulses,

palm oil and sugar under the Special Public

Distribution System which had been

launched by late Hon’ble Chief Minister

Kalaignar in 2007, has been streamlined

resulting in substantial cost savings to the

public exchequer.

27

37) This Government has constituted

a committee chaired by Justice A.K.Rajan to

study the adverse impact of NEET on socially

and educationally backward students. Based

on the recommendations of the committee,

the Government will introduce necessary

legislation to ensure that the students of

Tamil Nadu are not adversely affected by

NEET and will take necessary steps to obtain

the consent of the Hon’ble President for such

legislation. The Anna Centenary Library

will be renovated and revitalised. Work on a

world-class public library in the name of the

late Hon’ble Chief Minister Kalaignar at

Madurai at a cost of Rs.70 crore will be

commenced shortly.

38) Consistent efforts will be made to

make education for children universal and

inclusive. Utmost priority will be given

28

to providing quality education for all children

studying in Government schools.

This Government will make all out efforts to

ensure Tamil Nadu reaches the top rank in

the Performance Grading Index (PGI)

brought out by the Ministry of Education,

Government of India by focusing on the

domain of Learning Outcomes and

Quality, where the State’s ranking was

pulled down in 2019-20. A mission mode

project that will ensure continuity of

education delivery will be implemented. ICT

will be leveraged, and refresher courses will

be delivered to children in order to make up

for learning losses during the pandemic

period.

39) Preserving lives and livelihoods

during the Covid pandemic has been the

priority of this Government. Accordingly,

29

factories and commercial establishments

have been allowed to function wherever

possible, strictly in accordance with

the standard operating procedures.

extracts.title: G. O (Ms) No. 44: Corona pandemic relief measures – Distribution of Grocery kits to the Rice Family Cardholders – Sanction of funds – Orders - issued.
extracts.text:
ABSTRACT

Corona pandemic relief measures — Distribution of Grocery kits to the Rice Family Cardholders — Sanction of funds — Orders - issued.

Co-operation, Food and Consumer Protection (F1) Department

G.O.(Ms) No.44 Dated: 29.05.2021 eve aihL1o, sneiesmrél —15 HHorsTEHout 9160015) 2052 Read:

4. From the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation, Chennai-10 Letter No.BS6/13913/2021, dated 11.05.2021.

2. From the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection, Letter No.E2/9925/2021, dated 12.05.2021.

ORDER:-

The Government of Tamil Nadu has announced complete lockdown in the State from 10.05.2021 to 24.05.2021 in view of Covid pandemic situation. In the letter first read above, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has stated that, in the meeting chaired by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu on 11.05.2021, it has been decided to distribute 14 grocery items with cloth bag to the Rice Family Cardholders, in order to secure the livelihood of the people affected during Covid pandemic situation.

2. In this regard, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has informed that, as per the decision taken in the meeting, for the distribution of 14 grocery items, such as, Wheat Flour, Salt, Rava, Sugar, Urad Dhal, Tamarind, etc., at an estimated cost of Rs.412.33 each to the 2,07,66,950 numbers of Rice Family Cardholders, a sum of Rs.856.28 crore is required. The Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has stated that, the above expenditure may vary after finalization of the tender to be floated by the TNCSC by following due procedures laid down in the Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 4998 and Rules 2000 for the purchase of the above commodities.

3. The Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has requested to sanction and release a sum of Rs.856.28 crore (Rupees eight hundred and fifty six crore and twenty eight lakh) immediately to the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to enable the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to procure and speedy distribution of Grocery items to the Rice Family Cardholders. Further, the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation has informed that, instead of adopting clause-16(a) of Tamil Nadu Transparency in Tenders Act, 4998 for the procurement of commodities by Tamil Nadu

2

Civil Supplies Corporation during this Covid pandemic emergency situation, TNCSC proposes to float short term tender to ensure transparency in procuring the commodities for Covid relief works.

4. In the letter second read above, the Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection has reported that, 2,15,00,062 Family Cards are in circulation. Out of which 2,11,12,798 Family Cards are Rice Family Cards (including Srilankan Refugees). The Commissioner of Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection has requested release of funds for the distribution of Grocery items under the head of Relief Measures for Disaster Management.

extracts.title: G. O (Ms) No. 44: Corona pandemic relief measures – Distribution of Grocery kits to the Rice Family Cardholders – Sanction of funds – Orders - issued.
extracts.text:
He has requested that, a sum of Rs.870.54 crore (2,11,12,798 X Rs.412.33 = Rs.870,54,39,999) may be sanctioned to enable the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to procure and distribute 2,11,12,798 number of Grocery kits to the Rice Family Cardholders as a relief measure during corona pandemic.

5. As the costing is only a tentative cost, the initial sanction has been limited to Rs.400/- per kit in anticipation of savings on selected items in the actual bidding. Further it is considered appropriate that, funds are released from Demand No.51 under Major Head “2945” as this is an item of COVID relief and eligible under SDRF as gratuitous immediate relief. Pending presentation of the main Budget 2021-2022, the requisite expenditure can initially be met from an advance from the Food Subsidy intended for the 2"? quarter of 2021-2022.

6. The Government after careful consideration pass the following orders:-

(i) A sum of Rs.844.51 crore (Rupees eight hundred and forty four crore and fifty one lakh only) (2,11,12,798 X Rs.400 = Rs.844,51,19,200) is sanctioned and released immediately to the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to enable the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to procure and distribute 2,11,12,798 Grocery kits (details of items per kit as annexed) to the Rice Family Cardholders as a relief measure during corona pandemic, by relaxing Quarterly Control of Appropriation system for which orders were issued in the Government Letter No.15417/Fin(BG-l)Dept./2021-1, dated 30.03.2021. Further, this QCA relaxation is included in the online Quarterly Control of Appropriation (QCA) module of IFHRMS also, to facilitate drawal bills under IFHRMS as well.

(ii) Permission to the Managing Director, Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation to float short term tender for the procurement of commodities for Grocery items during this Covid pandemic emergency situation.

(iii) Release of funds from Demand No.51 under Major Head “2245” as this is an item of COVID relief and eligible under SDRF as gratuitous immediate relief. A specific inclusion within these norms should be taken up by Revenue Department as this is an unprecedented calamity.

(iv) Pending presentation of the main Budget 2021-2022, the requisite expenditure shall be initially met from an advance from the Food Subsidy intended for the 2" quarter of 2021-2022

7. The amount sanctioned in para 6 above shall be debited to the following Head of Account:- “3456-00 Civil Supplies 103 Consumer Subsidies — State’s Expenditure — AE Social Safety Net — Food Security - PDS Support — 317 Subsidies — 02 General Subsidy”

extracts.title: G.O Ms.No. 160: MEDICAL AID – New Health Insurance Scheme, 2021 – Provision of Health Care Assistance to the Employees of Government Departments, State Public Sector Undertakings, Statutory Boards, Local Bodies, State Government Universities etc., and their eligible family members through the United India Insurance Company Limited, Chennai Implementation - Orders – Issued.
extracts.text:
During the interim period of preparation and distribution of the identity cards, the Insurance Company shall authorise acceptance of the identity cards already issued under NHIS, 2016 as valid identity for the purpose of availing the Scheme. This arrangement will be applicable only for such interim period, till the identity cards are made available.

(ii) The Insurance Company shall arrange to issue identity cards to

the existing Employees and their eligible family members of Government Departments etc., under the scope of the Scheme. The DDO shall arrange to furnish the data of such Employees and their eligible family members of Government Departments etc., as in Annexure-III. The data furnished by the State Government shall be the property of the State Government and should not be used for any other purpose without the prior permission of the Government of Tamil Nadu.

14. Procedure to be followed by the Beneficiaries for availing Medical Assistance under this Scheme:

(1) In case of Planned Hospitalisation: The Beneficiaries seeking

medical assistance under this Scheme shall approach the Network Hospitals only for the approved treatments and surgeries to be undertaken on CASHLESS basis so that pre-authorisation is given by the Insurance Company / Third Party Administrator under the control of the Insurance Company.

(2) In case of Emergency Care or following an Accident:

The Beneficiary seeking medical assistance under this Scheme shall approach either Network Hospital for the approved treatments and surgeries to be undertaken on CASHLESS basis or Non-Network Hospital for the treatments and surgeries to be undertaken on reimbursement basis. The Beneficiary has to pay the medical expenses first directly to the hospital and then seek cash reimbursement for the approved treatments and surgeries

21

undertaken subject to Eligible Medical Expenses and Ceiling Criteria. There will be no cashless facility applicable in Non-Network Hospital.

(3) The Scheme is that ordinarily the Employees and their eligible

family members of Government Departments etc., is required to avail CASHLESS facility in Network Hospital (to the extent of Eligible Medical Expenses and Ceiling Criteria under the Scheme) and pay for non-medical expenses directly to the hospital.

(4) In case, Employees or their eligible family members of

Government Departments etc., undergo emergency treatments / surgeries not covered under this Scheme in either Network Hospital or Non-Network Hospital, no claim can be filed under the Health Insurance Scheme. However, they shall be eligible for claim to the extent permissible under the Tamil Nadu Medical Attendance Rules and the G.O.Ms.No.1023, Health and Family Welfare Department, dated 17-06-1980. It may be noted that the Tamil Nadu Medical Attendance Rules requires that treatment in private hospitals should not be resorted to except in cases of emergencies. Clause 2(3) of the aforesaid G.O. states that in genuine cases of emergency, the claims will be restricted to the expenditure that would have been incurred had the patient taken treatment in a Government hospital excepting diet charges.
